title: Launch self-serve Federated Evidence Exchange and Insurance Offset experiment for procurement
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce time-to-contract and underwriting friction for enterprise procurement by launching a self-serve Federated Evidence Exchange (FEE) that lets vendors push vetted attestations and SOC2 artifacts directly into Redwood's procurement portal, combined with an Insurance Offset Calculator (IOC) experiment that dynamically suggests insurance crediting for contract pricing.

Background: Procurement friction remains a top blocker for enterprise conversions. We currently operate a manual evidence intake flow that requires legal and finance back-and-forth and results in >6 week mean time to onboard for high-risk vendors. The FEE aims to automate accepted evidence ingestion (signed attestations, SOC2 letter, insurance declarations, KYC docs) via secure connectors and signed manifests. IOC is a pricing/packaging experiment that models how vendor-held insurance should reduce Redwood's compliance premium and offer a contract-level credit.

Scope: MVP includes (1) an opt-in vendor portal endpoint for uploading signed PDFs and S3 manifests, (2) a minimal federation API for partner assurance providers to push pre-validated attestations, (3) server-side validation ruleset for SOC2 presence, insurance minimums, and date ranges, and (4) the IOC UI in the procurement console that surfaces a suggested credit and shows rationale. Excludes full manual underwriting or policy negotiation in MVP — those remain handled by Legal.

Success metrics: median vendor onboarding time reduced from 42 days to <=14 days for vendors that use FEE; conversion lift of +8% for enterprise signings; percentage of uploads auto-validated >= 70%; IOC acceptance rate (legal signs off on suggested credit) >= 30% in pilot.

Trade-offs and risks: automation reduces manual effort but risks false acceptance of expired or forged docs — mitigated by signed-manifest requirements, SHA checksum verification, and sampling audits. Tightening validation rules improves safety but increases false negatives and support tickets. IOC can materially affect contract economics; to reduce risk we will cap credits to a bounded amount during pilot and require manual legal approval for credits > threshold. Data privacy: all uploaded artifacts are stored in a customer-scoped encrypted bucket and retention follows the procurement retention policy.

Rollout plan: run a 6-week pilot with three channel partners and five strategic customers, monitor key signals, iterate validation rules, and hand off to Dedicated/Private sales motions if successful.

Stakeholders: Product (Priya), Engineering (Javier), Legal (Marcus Chen), Security/Compliance (Alice Nguyen), Solutions Eng (Leila Hassan).
acceptance_criteria: FEE API accepts and records signed-manifest uploads with checksum verification
Automated validator flags missing or expired SOC2/insurance and returns actionable error codes
IOC displays suggested credit and a clear rationale in procurement UI for pilot customers
Audit log entries capture uploader identity, timestamp, and validation outcome for every artifact
Pilot onboarding time metric tracked and reportable in procurement dashboard
